title: Next.js hydration mismatch error caused by browser-only code in component render

error.message: Error: Hydration failed because the initial UI does not match what was rendered on the server.
error.context: A Next.js page component accesses window.innerWidth directly in the render body to conditionally render a mobile vs desktop layout. Works in development but throws hydration error in production because the server render has no window object.

solution.description: Moved all browser-only code (window, document, localStorage access) into a useEffect hook that only runs client-side. Used a mounted state flag to prevent rendering browser-dependent UI until after hydration is complete.
steps: Identify the component accessing browser APIs (window, document, localStorage) in the render path
Add a 'mounted' state that starts as false
Move all browser API access into a useEffect hook
Only render the browser-dependent UI after mounted is true
Provide a reasonable default/fallback for the server render
Test by disabling JavaScript in the browser to verify the SSR output is valid HTML
